newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone nets 53,000 new customers in UK.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone nets 53,000 new customers in UK.

text.p: Vodafone Group Plc, Britain's biggest mobile telephone company, said on Tuesday it had won 53,000 net new subscribers in Britain in the second quarter of the year.
Its overseas operations also added more than 182,000 net new customers with continued strong performances in Greece, South Africa, France and The Netherlands, the group added in a statement
Vodafone said its subscriber base at the end of June was 2.92 million in Britain and its share of overseas markets was over 1.33 million.

Chief executive Chris Gent said that exceptional levels of churn -- when customers cancel subscriptions -- after the company reduced its customer contracts to 12 from 15 months, had depressed UK net connections by 35,000 in the quarter.
"With this now out of the way, the UK growth coupled with our excellent overseas connections sees us well on track to connect a million net new customers in the year," he added.
Orange Plc, Britain's youngest mobile telephone company, has outstripped its rivals so far, connecting 86,000 net new subscribers in the quarter.
Cellnet, 60-percent owned by British Telecommunications Plc, said it had added 74,000 in the quarter.
